title: Main Stage Soundcheck
summary: Soundcheck a festival stage: ride a fader to set the capacitor, coil, master voltage and bass note, then drop the beat.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 7.6, AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
learningOutcome: The student can find the impedance, current and phase of series RC and LCR circuits, add voltages as phasors, and use cos φ = R/Z for the power in a real coil.

levels.title: Tweeter and capacitor
levels.adds: Baseline: in a series RC circuit Z = √(R² + X_C²), and V_R + V_C exceeds the source voltage (Example 7.6).
hints: Z = V/I = √(R² + X_C²), not R + X_C.
More capacitance means less X_C and more current.

levels.title: The mid driver
levels.adds: New idea: Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R; lagging or leading current (Example 7.8).
hints: Subtract X_C from X_L before squaring.
If X_L is bigger the current lags; if X_C is bigger it leads.
Two coil settings give one current: only one has the asked phase.

levels.title: Back to the master
levels.adds: More steps: the three voltages add as phasors, V = √(V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²) (Section 7.6.1).
hints: V_L and V_C are opposite in phase, so subtract them.
V_R is a quarter cycle from the difference.
Combine with Pythagoras; do not add all three.

levels.title: The woofer’s real coil
levels.adds: Apply it: a coil is a resistor in series with an inductor; only R dissipates, P = I²R, power factor cos φ = R/Z (Section 7.7).
hints: From P = I²R find the current, then Z = V/I.
X_L = √(Z² − R²) and X_L = 2πfL with L in henry.
The power factor is cos φ = R/Z.

misconceptions: Impedance is the sum R + X_L + X_C
The voltages across R, L and C add up arithmetically to the source voltage
The reactances of L and C add
